OperationalDesignDomain.desc: The complete set of conditions under which the automated driving system is designed to operate.

Environment.desc: Atmospheric and ambient conditions that affect driving and sensing.

Weather.desc: Overall atmospheric conditions at the time of driving.

Clear.desc: Weather condition with no significant clouds or precipitation.

Cloudy.desc: Weather condition with significant cloud cover.

Rain.desc: Liquid water precipitation in various intensities.

Snow.desc: Frozen water precipitation in the form of snowflakes.

Sleet.desc: Mixed precipitation of rain and snow.

Hail.desc: Precipitation in the form of balls or irregular lumps of ice.

Storm.desc: Violent atmospheric disturbance with strong wind and precipitation.

Illumination.desc: Lighting conditions affecting visibility and sensor performance.

Twilight.desc: Soft glowing light before sunrise and after sunset.

ArtificialLight.desc: Lighting provided by man-made sources such as street lamps.

Precipitation.desc: Intensity level of any moisture falling from the atmosphere.

Fog.desc: Visible mass of condensed water vapor in the atmosphere, reducing visibility.

LightFog.desc: Thin fog with minor visibility reduction.

MediumFog.desc: Moderate fog with significant visibility reduction.

DenseFog.desc: Thick fog with severe visibility reduction.

Temperature.desc: Degree of heat present in the environment and on road surfaces.

Wind.desc: Movement of air, which may affect vehicle stability and sensors.

AirQuality.desc: Chemical and particulate composition of ambient air.

Color.desc: Visual color of vehicles, road elements, or environmental features.

White.desc: Color of maximum lightness, often used for emergency vehicles or high visibility.

Black.desc: Color of minimum lightness, common for vehicles and road surfaces.

Gray.desc: Achromatic color between black and white, frequently seen on vehicles and pavement.

Silver.desc: Metallic gray color with reflective sheen, popular for automotive paint.

Red.desc: Warm color associated with stop signals, brake lights, and emergency vehicles.

Blue.desc: Cool color used for some emergency lights and commercial vehicle markings.

Green.desc: Color indicating go signals, directional signs, and environmental features.

Yellow.desc: High-visibility color for warning signs, school buses, and caution markings.

Brown.desc: Earthy color common for cargo vehicles and roadside natural features.

Maroon.desc: Dark reddish-brown color, occasionally used for vehicle paint.

Purple.desc: Rare vehicle color, sometimes seen on specialized or custom vehicles.

Dark.desc: Low-luminance color attribute, often used to describe black, navy, or charcoal tones.

Light.desc: High-luminance color attribute, such as light blue or light gray.

Golden.desc: Metallic yellow-brown color, sometimes used for luxury or decorative vehicles.

Taupe.desc: Brownish-gray color, occasionally seen on vehicles as a neutral tone.

Orange.desc: High-visibility color used for construction vehicles and warning equipment.

Pink.desc: Uncommon vehicle color, sometimes used for promotional or specialty vehicles.

Road.desc: Physical characteristics and conditions of the roadway.

Highway.desc: Major road designed for high-speed through traffic.

UrbanRoad.desc: Road located within a city or urbanized area.

RuralRoad.desc: Road in countryside or low-density areas.

ResidentialRoad.desc: Road within a residential zone with low speed limits.

ServiceRoad.desc: Road providing access to properties or facilities.

RoadGeometry.desc: Horizontal and vertical shape of the road, including curves and slopes.

Straight.desc: Road segment with no curvature or minimal deviation from a straight line.

Curved.desc: Road segment with a continuous bend or arc.

Wide.desc: Road with extra lane width or generous shoulder area.

Narrow.desc: Road with reduced lane width or limited clearance.

Slight.desc: Road with a gentle curve or shallow slope.

RoadSurface.desc: Physical condition and texture of the road surface.

Potholes.desc: Road surface with structural defects and holes.

LaneMarkings.desc: Paint or physical markings defining lanes and traffic rules.

RoadConditions.desc: Overall state of the road including defects, construction, and obstacles.

Shoulder.desc: Area beside the main travel lanes for emergency stopping.

Intersection.desc: Point where two or more roads cross or meet.

Bridge.desc: Structure carrying road over an obstacle such as water or valley.

Tunnel.desc: Enclosed passage for road through a hill or mountain.

RoadAttribute.desc: Adjective attributes describing traffic or environmental state of the road.

Main.desc: Primary or arterial road that carries significant traffic volume.

Busy.desc: Road with high traffic density or frequent interruptions.

Empty.desc: Road with very few or no other road users.

Curvy.desc: Road characterized by multiple successive curves or winding alignment.

Shadowed.desc: Road section where sunlight is blocked by buildings, trees, or structures.

Traffic.desc: Conditions related to other road users and traffic regulation.

TrafficParticipants.desc: All actors present in the driving environment.

EmergencyVehicle.desc: Vehicle used for emergency services such as police, fire, ambulance.

PoliceCar.desc: Law enforcement vehicle with emergency lights and sirens.

Ambulance.desc: Medical emergency vehicle equipped for patient transport.

FireTruck.desc: Firefighting vehicle with water, ladders, and emergency equipment.

SchoolBus.desc: Bus dedicated to transporting students, typically painted yellow.

SUV.desc: Sport utility vehicle, a car-like body on a truck chassis.

Sedan.desc: Three-box passenger car with separate compartments for engine, passenger, and cargo.

Pickup.desc: Light truck with an open cargo bed and enclosed cab.

Wagon.desc: Station wagon with extended roofline and rear cargo area.

Hatchback.desc: Car with a rear door that swings upward, combining passenger and cargo space.

Coupe.desc: Two-door passenger car with a sporty or sleek profile.

Minivan.desc: Multi-purpose vehicle designed for passenger transport with sliding doors.

MPV.desc: Multi-purpose vehicle, similar to a minivan, for flexible passenger/cargo use.

Crossover.desc: Vehicle built on a car platform with SUV-like styling and height.

Jeep.desc: Off-road capable vehicle, often with four-wheel drive and rugged design.

Van.desc: Boxy vehicle designed for cargo or passenger transport, often commercial.

Taxi.desc: Licensed vehicle for hire, typically with distinctive markings.

Brand.desc: Manufacturer or model brand of a vehicle.

Ford.desc: American automaker producing a wide range of vehicles.

Dodge.desc: American brand known for trucks, muscle cars, and SUVs.

Audi.desc: German premium automaker under the Volkswagen Group.

Toyota.desc: Japanese automaker, one of the largest in the world.

Suburu.desc: Japanese automaker known for all-wheel-drive vehicles.

Forester.desc: Subaru model, a compact crossover SUV.

Mustang.desc: Ford model, a iconic American muscle car.

Journey.desc: Dodge model, a mid-size crossover SUV.

Chevvy.desc: Informal name for Chevrolet, an American brand.

VulnerableRoadUser.desc: Road users with little or no protection, at high risk in collisions.

Animal.desc: Domestic or wild animals on or near the road.

Obstacle.desc: Any non-living object that may obstruct the path of a vehicle, such as debris or construction equipment.

Cargo.desc: Goods or freight being transported, either inside or attached to a vehicle.

Trailer.desc: Unpowered vehicle towed by a powered vehicle, used for hauling cargo.

TrafficFlow.desc: Movement characteristics of traffic over time.

TrafficDensity.desc: Concentration of vehicles per unit length of road.

TrafficRules.desc: Formal rules governing right-of-way, overtaking, turning, etc.

TrafficSigns.desc: Visual signs providing regulatory, warning, or guidance information.

TrafficSignals.desc: Electric signals controlling right-of-way at intersections.

SpatialRelation.desc: Relative positions and orientations between traffic participants or between vehicle and road elements.

Behind.desc: Located at the rear of a reference object.

Ahead.desc: Located in front of the reference vehicle along its direction of travel.

Left.desc: Located on the left-hand side of a reference point.

Right.desc: Located on the right-hand side of a reference point.

Front.desc: Located in front of a reference object, often the forward-facing side.

Side.desc: Lateral region adjacent to a vehicle or object.

Opposite.desc: Facing directly towards or positioned on the other side of the road.

Along.desc: Moving or positioned parallel to a line or road.

Past.desc: Position beyond a reference point after passing it.

Across.desc: From one side to the other, traversing a road or intersection.

Onto.desc: Moving to a position on a road or surface.

Towards.desc: In the direction of a target or object.

Around.desc: Surrounding or encircling an object or area.

Beside.desc: Next to or alongside a reference object.

Nearby.desc: Within a short distance of a reference point.

Next.desc: Immediately adjacent or following in sequence.

Forward.desc: Ahead direction, along the vehicle's heading.

Aside.desc: To the side; out of the main path.

Alongside.desc: Parallel and adjacent to a vehicle or road feature.

TrafficCondition.desc: State of traffic including density, disruptions, and special events.

Congestion.desc: Heavy traffic with low speeds and stop-and-go conditions.

Flow.desc: Smooth, uninterrupted movement of vehicles at optimal speeds.

Group.desc: A cluster of vehicles traveling closely together.

Row.desc: A line of vehicles, often waiting at a signal or in a queue.

Accident.desc: Collision or incident involving vehicles, requiring response and causing disruption.

Construction.desc: Road work zone with temporary lane closures, equipment, and workers.

IllegalParking.desc: Vehicles parked in prohibited areas, obstructing traffic or safety.

DrivingDynamics.desc: Dynamic behavior of the vehicle during operation.

Speed.desc: Rate of motion of the vehicle.

LateralMovement.desc: Side-to-side motion including lane changes and steering.

Stopping.desc: Conditions and events related to vehicle stopping.

VehicleState.desc: Temporal states and maneuvers of a vehicle during operation.

Parked.desc: Vehicle stationary in a designated parking space or off-road.

Stopped.desc: Vehicle at a standstill, e.g., at a traffic light or stop sign.

Moving.desc: Vehicle in motion at any speed above zero.

Speeding.desc: Vehicle exceeding the posted speed limit.

Waiting.desc: Vehicle paused, typically for a traffic signal, pedestrian, or gap.

Yielding.desc: Vehicle giving right-of-way to other traffic or pedestrians.

Slowing.desc: Vehicle reducing speed, not necessarily to a full stop.

Pulling.desc: Vehicle moving away from a stop or curb, often pulling out.

Overtaking.desc: Vehicle passing another vehicle in the same direction.

Passing.desc: Vehicle moving past another road user or obstacle.

Merging.desc: Vehicle entering a stream of traffic from a ramp or lane.

Switching.desc: Vehicle changing lanes or turning direction.

Changing.desc: Vehicle performing a lane change or direction change.

Crossing.desc: Vehicle traversing an intersection or railroad crossing.

Turning.desc: Vehicle changing direction at an intersection or junction.

Going.desc: Vehicle proceeding in a general direction without specific maneuver.

Driving.desc: Vehicle operating under normal forward motion.

Running.desc: Vehicle actively moving, often at a steady pace.

Following.desc: Vehicle traveling behind another vehicle, maintaining distance.

Keeping.desc: Vehicle maintaining a steady speed or lane position.

Proceeding.desc: Vehicle moving forward after a stop or hesitation.

Continuing.desc: Vehicle persisting in its current path without change.

Traveling.desc: Vehicle on a journey, covering distance along a route.

Entering.desc: Vehicle moving into a new road, lane, or intersection.

Exiting.desc: Vehicle leaving a road, roundabout, or parking area.

Taking.desc: Vehicle executing a specific action, such as a turn or lane.

Making.desc: Vehicle performing a maneuver, e.g., making a turn.

Rounding.desc: Vehicle navigating a curve or roundabout.

Beginning.desc: Vehicle starting a new movement or maneuver.

Disappearing.desc: Vehicle leaving the sensor field of view or occluded.

Infrastructure.desc: Fixed physical structures supporting road safety and control.

TrafficLight.desc: Signal device controlling vehicle and pedestrian flow.

TrafficSign.desc: Permanent or temporary sign conveying traffic information.

GuardRail.desc: Barrier preventing vehicles from leaving the roadway.

Crosswalk.desc: Designated area for pedestrians to cross the road.

RailroadCrossing.desc: Point where road and railway intersect.

Streetlight.desc: Pole-mounted lamp providing illumination on roads and sidewalks.

BikeRack.desc: Fixed structure for securing parked bicycles.

TemporalConditions.desc: Time-related factors affecting traffic and environment.

TimeOfDay.desc: Time segment during the day (e.g., morning, evening).

Season.desc: Period of the year (spring, summer, autumn, winter).

Holiday.desc: Public or local holiday affecting traffic patterns.

SpecialEvent.desc: Planned event causing abnormal traffic or environment.

LegalRegulatoryConditions.desc: Laws and regulations governing driving in the region.

SpeedLimits.desc: Legally imposed maximum and minimum speeds.

RightOfWayRules.desc: Rules determining which traffic has priority.

OvertakingRules.desc: Rules governing overtaking and passing maneuvers.

ParkingRules.desc: Rules about where and how parking is permitted.

RegionalLegislation.desc: Local or national laws specific to the operating region.

VehicleCapabilities.desc: Performance and functional limits of the subject vehicle.

AutonomyLevel.desc: Level of driving automation according to standards.

SensorSuite.desc: Set of sensors installed on the vehicle.

ActuatorPerformance.desc: Performance limits of steering, throttle, and braking systems.

VehicleSize.desc: Physical dimensions and mass category of the vehicle.

Small.desc: Compact vehicle with small footprint, easy to maneuver.

Large.desc: Full-size vehicle with extended dimensions and mass.

Midsize.desc: Intermediate vehicle size between compact and full-size.

Big.desc: Large vehicle, often used for SUVs and trucks.

Tiny.desc: Very small vehicle such as microcar or urban quadricycle.

Huge.desc: Extra-large vehicle, e.g., heavy-duty truck or bus.

Perception.desc: System ability to detect and recognize objects and features.

VisibilityRange.desc: Maximum distance at which objects can be detected.

ObstacleDetection.desc: Ability to detect obstacles of various types and sizes.

LaneRecognition.desc: Ability to recognize lane boundaries and markings.

SignRecognition.desc: Ability to detect and interpret traffic signs.

Map.desc: Digital map characteristics used by the automated system.

MapCoverage.desc: Geographic area covered by the map.

MapType.desc: Format and representation type of the map.

LaneLevelMap.desc: Map containing detailed lane-level geometry and attributes.
